setup: Container off the ship, off the paperwork, a bought forklift driver and a fifteen-minute gap in the yard's camera loop that cost more than a car.
on_success: Off the stack, onto the flatbed, through the gate on the driver's pass during the loop. The sea never happened.
on_fail: The gap in the loop was fifteen minutes yesterday. Today it's nothing, and the driver's phone is off.
on_crit: Extra crate wedged behind the declared load that even the plug forgot to mention.

setup: RIB on a dark beach, cargo double-wrapped and buoyant, a tide table memorised and a coastguard shift you've timed to the minute.
on_success: In on the high water, unload to the van up the slipway, back out before the tide turns and the patrol comes round.
on_fail: Tide's wrong, engine floods, and a dog walker who couldn't sleep is already on the phone describing your torch.
on_crit: Sea was flat, run was fast, and there was more in the wrap than the weight you paid for.

target.detail: the container that walked off the manifest

setup: A container off the ship and off the paperwork, a bought forklift driver, and a fifteen-minute gap in the yard's camera loop that cost more than a car and lasts exactly as long as it was paid to.
on_success: Off the stack, onto the flatbed, through the gate on the driver's pass during the loop. As far as the sea's concerned, this box never crossed it.
on_fail: The gap in the loop was fifteen minutes yesterday. Tonight it's nothing, and the driver's phone is off, and you're stood in a lit yard.
on_crit: There's an extra crate wedged behind the declared load that even the plug forgot to mention. Finders keepers, at these prices.

target.detail: the RIB coming in on the high tide

setup: A dark beach, cargo double-wrapped and floating, a tide table memorised to the minute, and a coastguard shift you've timed twice to be sure. The sea does half the work if you read it right.
on_success: In on the high water, unloaded to the van up the slipway, and back out before the tide turns and the patrol comes round the headland.
on_fail: The tide's wrong, the engine floods, and a dog walker who couldn't sleep is already describing your torch to somebody official.

setup: A ferry, a foot passenger with an ordinary bag and an ordinary face, and a lining sewn just right. Cars get searched; people with return tickets and boring shoes mostly don't.
on_success: Walk on, walk off, nothing in the hold to find because it's all in the lining and the lining's all in a bag that looks like a hundred others.
on_fail: There's a spot-check today because someone got greedy last week, and the dog by the ramp doesn't care how boring your shoes are.
on_crit: You're waved through so fast you could've carried twice as much, and next time, God help you, you probably will.

target.detail: the refrigerated lorry with a false floor under the fish boxes

setup: A reefer full of fish boxes off the docks, a false floor under the pallets, a driver on the payroll, and a customs check that mostly waves cold, smelly loads straight through because nobody wants to unpack fish.
on_success: The check leans in, gets a face full of week-old cod, waves it on. The floor stays a floor. The driver stays calm. Everyone stays out of prison.
on_fail: The one keen officer on the shift decides today's the day he unpacks a fish lorry, and the false floor is exactly false enough to notice.

target.detail: the grass strip out past the farms with the landing lights on a timer

setup: A private grass strip, a light aircraft that files no plan, landing lights on a timer, and a farmer who's decided his fields earn more in ten minutes at night than in a year of subsidies.
on_success: Wheels down, engine barely off, cargo swapped to the Land Rover and the plane's a dot again before the timer kills the lights.
on_fail: There's a plane on the radar that shouldn't be, a coastguard controller having a slow night, and a police helicopter that's already turning.

target.name: Sandra
target.detail: the retired couple's motorhome with the extra tank

setup: A motorhome coming off the tunnel, a grey-haired couple with a folder of campsite bookings, and a water tank that holds a good deal more than water. Nobody strip-searches a caravan full of pensioners.
on_success: They ask about the weather in France, wave the folder, get waved through. The 'water tank' gets pumped out in a lay-by twenty miles on.
on_fail: A new officer follows the training to the letter, taps the tank, hears the wrong kind of hollow, and asks them to pull into bay three.

target.detail: the parcels posted to a dozen empty addresses

setup: Small dear things broken across a dozen packages, posted to a dozen addresses that are all empty flats with working letterboxes, so no single parcel is worth a search and no single address means a thing.
on_success: The postal system does the smuggling for you, one harmless little box at a time, and you collect the set from a round of empty hallways.
on_fail: One address gets flagged for a different reason entirely, and a routine visit turns up a mat piled with parcels that all want explaining.

target.detail: the holdall you're carrying for the first time and can feel the weight of

setup: Your first proper run, a holdall that weighs nothing and everything, a service station rendezvous, and the specific terror of standing in a bright shop pretending to choose a meal deal while carrying a decade.
on_success: You buy the meal deal you don't want, meet the car you're supposed to, hand it over, and get in your own car with hands that won't quite stop.
on_fail: You clock a patrol car in the services and freeze for exactly one second too long, and a bored officer notices a man being that still.
